# 2B.2 Research Note: Olaf Scholz in 2024

**Bottom line:** I found **no reliable evidence** that Scholz initiated or justified wars of choice, annexation, covert destabilization, or proxy conflict beyond defensive necessity in 2024. The record is instead dominated by **defensive support for Ukraine, escalation restraint, and de-escalation in other crises**. The only real counterweight is continued arms support and deterrence, which may prolong a defensive war, but the available evidence frames that as necessary support rather than offensive expansion.

## Accepted claim items

| Type | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Strongly exculpatory | **Scholz im Interview mit der taz** | Bundesregierung | 13 Apr 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-de/aktuelles/scholz-interview-in-der-taz-2270696 | Scholz said fear of escalation is understandable, rejected a quick endgame by force, and framed support for Ukraine as necessary to prevent Russian victory. This is direct evidence against a war-of-choice posture and for defensive necessity. | 2B.2, 1B.1, 2B.1, 1B.8 |
| Strongly exculpatory | **Questions orales au gouvernement mars 2024** | Bundesregierung | 4 Mar 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-fr/service/archives/chancelier-questions-2024-2265010 | Scholz refused Taurus delivery because German soldiers would have to be involved and he did not want Germany drawn into the war. This is strong evidence against proxy-conflict expansion and against using force beyond defensive necessity. | 2B.2, 1B.1, 1B.5, 2B.1 |
| Strongly exculpatory | **Le gouvernement fédéral s’efforce de parvenir à une désescalade** | Bundesregierung | 15 Apr 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-fr/service/archives/declaration-chancelier-iran-2270888 | After Iran’s attack on Israel, Scholz and the German government emphasized de-escalation and avoiding a regional conflagration. This is crisis evidence against broadening conflict beyond defensive necessity. | 2B.2, 1B.8, 2B.1 |
| Strongly exculpatory | **Speech by Federal Chancellor Olaf Scholz at the Munich Security Conference** | Federal Government | 17 Feb 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-en/service/archive/speech-by-federal-chancellor-olaf-scholz-at-the-munich-security-conference-2260378 | Scholz said Germany and its partners did not want a conflict between Russia and NATO and reiterated that no German troops would be sent to Ukraine. This is clear evidence against offensive escalation or proxy warfare. | 2B.2, 1B.2, 2B.1 |
| Exculpatory | **Rede von Bundeskanzler Olaf Scholz** | Bundesregierung | 4 Dec 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-de/suche/rede-von-bundeskanzler-olaf-scholz-2323758 | Scholz framed continued support for Ukraine as necessary for independence and sovereignty. This supports the view that Germany’s role was defensive support, not war expansion. | 2B.2, 1B.1, 2B.1 |
| Exculpatory | **Federal Chancellor Scholz’ press conference at the NATO Summit** | Federal Government | 11 Jul 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-en/service/archive/pc-chancellor-nato-summit-2298906 | Scholz defended the stationing of U.S. conventional weapons as part of deterrence and defense, while the page notes NATO coordination for Ukraine support. This is borderline, but still presented as war prevention rather than aggression. | 2B.2, 1B.5, 1B.4, 2B.1 |
| Borderline / mixed | **The Federal Chancellor’s 2024 summer press conference “I look forward to your questions”** | Federal Government | 24 Jul 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-en/service/archive/chancellor-summer-press-conference-2024-2301040 | Scholz said long-range U.S. weapons in Germany were meant to protect Germany and NATO and prevent war, while also saying Russia had violated arms-control agreements. This is not evidence of offensive war-making, but it is the closest item to a counterweight because it endorses forward deterrence. | 2B.2, 1B.4, 1B.5, 1B.6 |

## Counterevidence / limitations

- I found **no credible evidence** of Scholz pursuing annexation, covert destabilization, or proxy conflict beyond defensive necessity.
- I also found **no evidence** that he justified war as a preferred tool of statecraft.
- The closest borderline material is continued military support to Ukraine and NATO deterrence, but the record consistently frames that as **defense, restraint, and prevention of Russian victory**, not as an offensive war of choice.

## Synthesis for 2B.2

- **Most supported reading:** Scholz did **not** initiate or expand wars of choice or proxy conflict beyond defensive necessity in 2024.
- **Why:** his public record repeatedly emphasizes avoiding direct German entry into war, preventing escalation, and supporting partners defensively.
- **Main caveat:** Germany’s military aid to Ukraine does prolong the war in a broad sense, but the available evidence does not show it was pursued beyond defensive necessity or for offensive geopolitical gain.
